rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.read: Another Fed official, Kansas City's Jeff Schmid, warned that inflation is moving the wrong way, and a December Fed hike now looks all but certain. In Japan, board member Hajime Takata called for an early hike despite a shrinking economy. Europe, Britain and Japan are also expected to hike, but US rates are rising faster, which keeps favouring the dollar.
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~92–94% 25bp / ~6–8% 50bp (CME FedWatch, futures via Reuters); ECB Dec ~88%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~70–75%; BoC Dec ~32–36%

rows.title: Growth
rows.read: Japan's economy shrank slightly in the summer and China's October spending and factory figures all fell short. Neither moved currencies much, but weaker Chinese demand is a quiet drag on the Aussie and kiwi. The US economy still looks firmer, and US retail sales on Tuesday are the next check.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: US inflation is still running far above the Fed's goal, which keeps the pressure to hike and supports the dollar. Canada's October inflation this morning decides whether a December Bank of Canada hike comes back into view. UK inflation on Wednesday matters just as much for the pound.
rows.figure: Canada CPI Oct fcst ~3.0% y/y (Sep 3.1%), 7:30 AM CT today; UK CPI Oct fcst 3.6% (Sep 3.5%), Wed 1:00 AM CT; US PPI Oct +6.5% y/y

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: Iran's weekend claims of a sunk supertanker and strikes in Bahrain went unconfirmed, and US stock futures rose at the open. With markets calm, the safe-haven franc and yen got no lift. The Aussie and kiwi, which track market mood and China, stayed near their lows.
rows.figure: AUD/USD ~0.676 (lowest since January); NZD/USD ~0.552; USD/CHF ~0.839 (Saturday feed); Reuters: Trump may pause strikes if Iran and the Houthis hold back

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.read: Oil slipped as traders trusted the forecast of a supply surplus more than unconfirmed war claims. Cheaper oil eases the strain on energy buyers like Japan and the euro area and takes a little support from the Canadian dollar. Gold faded back below $3,900, offering the Aussie little help.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro, and the dollar's run keeps paying them. Their large bet on the yen keeps losing money as it weakens. A delayed weekly report from US regulators is due this afternoon.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.read: Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs above 5%. Higher yields support the dollar for now, but a growing deficit is a worry if buyers start asking for more. France's debt troubles keep weighing on the euro.
rows.figure: US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.14%
